newsitem.title: UK: C&W to abandon German alliance - paper.
newsitem.headline: C&W to abandon German alliance - paper.

text.p: Telecoms group Cable and Wireless (C&W) wants to abandon its German alliance with utilities Veba AG and RWE AG, The Times newspaper reported in its early Monday edition.
C&W and Veba formed a strategic alliance in 1995 and the two groups last year agreed to bring RWE on board. Final contracts have been drawn up, but C&W so far declined to sign them.
The Times, which did not cite any sources, reported the British telecoms firm told its German partners it wants to leave the alliance.

The report follows comments from an RWE official, who told Reuters on Saturday C&W has been exploring the possibility of an alliance with one of its main competitors: the Global One venture of Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and Sprint Corp from the U.S.
Telecom firms across the world have been frantically teaming up in recent years as telecom markets are being opened up to competition. Europe drops the final barriers to full competition next year.
The Times said C&W has become increasingly concerned about the rising costs of comepeting with Deutsche Telekom, the dominant force in all of Germany's telecoms markets.
No one at C&W was available to comment on the newspaper report.
